newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says discussing key liberalisation measures.
newsitem.headline: Spain says discussing key liberalisation measures.

text.p: The Spanish government said on Friday it had discussed a bill which would reform and liberalise key sectors of the economy, particularly property and telecomunications.
Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said these measures extended a series of economic reforms proposed during last June.
The future telecommunications law will include the liberalisation of basic telephony, and a shift away from the government's control of the sector.
It will also affect local and regional television, Rato said.
He added that the property reform will be based on the idea that all unprotected land can be used for building and development.
The government will review the maximum price system for gas, studying measures to pass over part of the cost of possible inefficiencies in the distribution system to consumers.
Spain would also aim to deregulate the tobacco monopoly, Rato said.
The measures are planned to be approved during this year. -- Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340
